descripcion_es: be + past participle in the present simple and past simple; when and how to mention the agent with by.
resumen: The passive is formed with be in the corresponding tense + past participle. It is used when the action or the object matters more than who does it, or when we don't know who does it.

items: The object of the active sentence becomes the subject, and be agrees with it: The letters were sent (plural).
The agent is introduced with by only if it gives useful information: The Mona Lisa was painted by Leonardo.
The agent is left out if it is obvious, unknown or irrelevant: He was arrested (by the police, obviously).
It is often equivalent to the Spanish reflexive passive with “se”: English is spoken here = Spanish “Aquí se habla inglés”.

explicacion.texto: Irregular past participles are the main source of mistakes: built, written, sold, made, taken, given, found, held, paid, sent, known. Revise them before doing the exercises.

ejemplos.frase: Spanish is spoken in more than twenty countries.
ejemplos.traduccion: El español se habla en más de veinte países.

ejemplos.frase: The bridge was built in the nineteenth century.
ejemplos.traduccion: El puente se construyó en el siglo XIX.

ejemplos.frase: Breakfast is served from seven to ten.
ejemplos.traduccion: El desayuno se sirve de siete a diez.

ejemplos.frase: The novel was written by a young Chilean author.
ejemplos.traduccion: La novela la escribió un joven autor chileno.
Por suerte, no cancelaron nuestro vuelo.

errores_hispanohablantes.nota: The passive needs the past participle, not the infinitive.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: In this shop is sold fruit.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: Fruit is sold in this shop.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: The English passive needs a subject before the verb; do not copy the Spanish reflexive passive with “se”.
Be agrees with the new subject: plural, were.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the passive in the present simple.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the first row of the table: in the present simple the passive is am/is/are + past participle. The clue is that coffee does not grow anything; it is grown, and the sentence describes a general fact (present simple). Coffee is uncountable and takes a singular verb, so is. The past participle of grow is irregular: grown. It is equivalent to the Spanish reflexive passive “se cultiva”.
ejercicios.traduccion: El café se cultiva en Colombia y Brasil.

errores_previstos.explicacion: This is active: it would say that coffee grows something. You need be + past participle.
Grow is irregular: the past participle is grown, not growed.
Coffee is uncountable and takes the singular: is grown.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the passive in the past simple.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the second row of the table: in the past simple the passive is was/were + past participle. The clue is by Pedro Almodóvar, which introduces the agent and means that the subject (the film) receives the action; also, it is a finished event. Film is singular, so was. The regular past participle of direct is directed.
ejercicios.traduccion: La película la dirigió Pedro Almodóvar.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Without be it is active past and would say that the film directed something; was is missing.
After was you need the past participle, directed, not the infinitive.
The instruction asks for the past simple: was directed.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the passive in the past simple.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the agreement rule from the rules and key points: be agrees with the new subject. The clue is the plural subject two people, which requires were. The people did not injure anyone; they were injured, so the past participle injured is used. This is a typical use in the news, where the agent is not important.
ejercicios.traduccion: Dos personas resultaron heridas en el accidente.

errores_previstos.explicacion: People is plural: the verb be must be plural, were.
Without be it is active and would say that two people injured someone.
After were comes the past participle, injured.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the passive in the present simple.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the “Negative” row of the table: the negative goes on be (aren't / are not), followed by the past participle. The clue is the plural subject these products and the general meaning, which calls for the present simple. The past participle of sell is irregular: sold. Both the contracted and the full form are accepted, because both are correct and only the register changes.
ejercicios.traduccion: Estos productos no se venden en los supermercados.

errores_previstos.explicacion: This is active with do: it would say that the products do not sell. In the passive do is not used; you make be negative.
Sell is irregular: the past participle is sold.
The subject is plural (these products): aren't sold.

ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the agreement rule and the omission of an obvious agent (He was arrested, by the police, obviously). The clue is that the thieves receive the action, they do not perform it, and it is a plural subject. That is why it is were + arrested. The natural Spanish translation uses the impersonal third person plural “detuvieron”.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: The thieves receive the action and the subject is plural: were arrested.

por_opcion.arrested: Incorrect: it is active and would mean that the thieves arrested someone; it is also missing an object.
por_opcion.were arrested: Correct: past passive with plural be, agreeing with the thieves.
por_opcion.was arrested: Incorrect: it has the passive structure, but was is singular and the subject is plural.

ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the rule on the agent: in the passive, the agent is introduced with by when it gives useful information, as in The Mona Lisa was painted by Leonardo. The clue is that after the gap comes the person who did the writing. By is equivalent to Spanish “por” in the agent phrase.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: The agent of a passive is introduced with by.

por_opcion.by: Correct: it introduces the agent of the passive.
por_opcion.from: Incorrect: from shows origin (a letter from Shakespeare), not the author in a passive. It is a common literal translation of Spanish “de”.
por_opcion.of: Incorrect: of shows possession (a play of Shakespeare's) and does not introduce the agent.

ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the “Question” row of the table: in the passive, be and the subject are inverted, without do. The clue is the past participle made at the end and the plural subject these shoes; we are asking about a past fact, so were. The question follows the order question word + were + subject + past participle.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Past passive question: were + subject + past participle.

por_opcion.did: Incorrect: did is used with active verbs (Where did they make these shoes?); with made in the passive you need be.
por_opcion.were: Correct: past passive, plural because of these shoes.
por_opcion.are being: Incorrect: as well as describing a process in progress, it would put both auxiliaries before the subject, which English does not allow (it would be Where are these shoes being made?).

ejercicios.frase: The museum is visit by thousands of people every year.
respuestas: The museum is visited by thousands of people every year.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the basic structure of the passive, be + past participle, and the first typical mistake on the card: using the infinitive instead of the past participle. The clue is by thousands of people, which reveals a passive, and the form is is already there. The regular past participle visited is missing.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: You need the past participle: visited.
ejercicios.traduccion: Miles de personas visitan el museo cada año.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The museum is visit by thousands of people every year.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This copies the sentence without correcting it: after is, the past participle visited is missing.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The museum visits by thousands of people every year.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Removing is turns it into a meaningless active sentence; the passive needs be + past participle.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The museum is visiting by thousands of people every year.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Is visiting is active continuous; the passive needs the past participle visited.

ejercicios.frase: The windows was cleaned this morning.
respuestas: The windows were cleaned this morning.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the agreement rule: be agrees with the new subject, as in The letters were sent. The clue is windows, plural with -s. In the past, the plural of be is were. The past participle cleaned is already correct.
ejercicios.traduccion: Las ventanas se limpiaron esta mañana.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The windows was cleaned this morning.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This copies the sentence without correcting it: with a plural subject it is were.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The window were cleaned this morning.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It changes the subject to singular instead of correcting the verb, and it also leaves an agreement error.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The windows are cleaned this morning.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This morning, already over, requires the past: were.

ejercicios.enunciado: Rewrite the sentence in the passive without mentioning the agent.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the rule of leaving out the agent when it is unknown. The clue is someone, which gives no information. The object my wallet becomes the subject, be goes in the past singular (was) and the irregular past participle of steal, stolen, is added. Adding by someone would be grammatically correct but redundant.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: The agent (someone) is unknown: leave it out.

errores_previstos.respuesta: My wallet was stolen by someone.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The instruction says not to mention the agent: by someone adds nothing.
Stole is the past simple; the past participle is stolen.
A literal copy of Spanish “me robaron la cartera”: in English the subject goes before the verb.

ejercicios.enunciado: Rewrite the sentence in the passive.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the rule on the agent: by + agent only when it gives useful information, and here the author is exactly what matters. The clue is that Picasso is a specific, relevant name. Guernica becomes the subject, be goes in the past singular (was) and the past participle painted is added, followed by by Picasso.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: The agent is relevant: by Picasso.

errores_previstos.explicacion: The agent is introduced with by, not with from.
After was comes the past participle painted.
Here the agent is relevant and the instruction does not ask you to leave it out: by Picasso.

ejercicios.enunciado: Rewrite the sentence in the passive without mentioning the agent.
ejercicios.frase: They clean the offices every evening.
respuestas: The offices are cleaned every evening.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the “Present simple” row of the table and the rule of leaving out an irrelevant agent. The clue is every evening, which shows a habit and therefore the present simple, and they, an impersonal subject that gives no information. The offices is plural, so are; the past participle is cleaned.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Present simple: are + past participle; they gives no information.
ejercicios.traduccion: Las oficinas se limpian todas las tardes.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The offices are cleaned by them every evening.
errores_previstos.explicacion: By them adds nothing, and the instruction says not to mention the agent.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The offices is cleaned every evening.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Offices is plural: are.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The offices were cleaned every evening.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The active sentence is in the present (clean), so the passive is too: are cleaned.

ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the equivalence with the Spanish reflexive passive given on the card: English is spoken here = Spanish “Aquí se habla inglés”. The clue is that the words include is and the past participle spoken, so you build a passive with English as the subject. The order is subject + is + past participle + place. The question Is English spoken here, with be before the subject, is also valid.
ejercicios.traduccion: Aquí se habla inglés. (También: ¿Se habla inglés aquí?)

errores_previstos.explicacion: A literal copy of Spanish “aquí se habla inglés”: the English passive needs the subject before the verb.
The past participle goes after be: is spoken.

ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the second row of the table: past simple passive, was + past participle. The clue is the date 1200, which calls for the past, and the irregular past participle built among the words. The normal order is subject + was + past participle + time phrase; it is also correct to put the time phrase first: In 1200 the castle was built.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Subject + was + past participle + time phrase.

errores_previstos.explicacion: A literal copy of Spanish “en 1200 se construyó el castillo”: the subject must go before the verb.
The past participle goes after be: was built.

descripcion_larga_es: The passive voice in the present and past (is made, was built) is used to focus the sentence on what happens or on the object affected, not on who acts. It is very common in news, instructions, technical texts and descriptions of processes. Spanish speakers find it difficult because Spanish prefers the reflexive passive with “se” and because you need to master irregular past participles and the agreement of be.

contexto.que_es: It is the construction in which the object of the active sentence becomes the subject and the verb is formed with a conjugated form of be plus the past participle: They make cars here becomes Cars are made here. The agent, if mentioned, is introduced by by.
contexto.por_que_importa: It is essential for talking about processes, products, history and news, where what happened matters more than who did it. If you copy the Spanish structure with “se” or forget the past participle, the sentence becomes ungrammatical or incomprehensible. In a written exam, using it correctly shows control of the impersonal register.
contexto.cuando_se_usa: When the agent is unknown, obvious or irrelevant (My bike was stolen, He was arrested), or when the topic of the sentence is the object (The bridge was built in 1890). It is the natural translation of many Spanish sentences with “se”: Spanish “Aquí se habla inglés” is English is spoken here. Spanish speakers tend to write “Here is spoken English” or to forget the subject.
